# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 103 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 103 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_103_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 20

**1** "Lord," I said, "I want to ask one more thing." "What?" he said. "What are the stones taken from the deep and fitted into the tower — and who are the twenty men who carried them?" **2** "The stones from the deep," he said, "are the first — those who believed before the Son of God was revealed in the world. They went down into the water dead and came up alive, knowing the name of the Son of God; therefore they were brought up from the deep and fitted into the building of the tower. **3** They were already sealed before they went down. The twenty men who carried them are the apostles and teachers of the proclamation of the Son of God." **4** "But why did the virgins also carry the stones through the gate?" **5** "Because the virgins had to go first and carry the stones into the building; without the power of the virgins, these stones could not have been placed into the tower — there would have been no fulness of life in them." **6** Then he showed me again the great banquet of the Son of God, with all the elect gathered at the table. **7** And the tall man — the Son of God — moved about among them rejoicing greatly, and the whole tower was full of the joy of the Lord. **8** The twelve virgins danced around the tower. When I asked what the great banquet was, he said, "This is the joy of the Lord at the completion of the tower."

---

*LOGOS: the retroactive sealing/baptism of the pre-Christian righteous (v. 2-3) is a remarkable early instance of the theology of salvation for those who died before Christ.*
